paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of and by language family. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect, measured in arbitrary units, of four different multilingual BERT model variants—mBERT-targ (light blue), XLM-targ (dark blue), mBERT-permute (light green), and XLM-permute (dark green)—across nine distinct language families or groups: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The horizontal axis lists these language families in alphabetical order, while the vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to 40 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each group of four bars represents one language family, with each bar corresponding to one model variant and its height indicating the mean effect value, accompanied by a vertical error bar representing the standard deviation. For example, in the IE-Baltic group, the mBERT-targ bar reaches approximately 22, the XLM-targ bar is around 16, the mBERT-permute bar is approximately 6, and the XLM-permute bar is about 5. In the Isolate group, the mBERT-targ bar is the tallest at approximately 35, while the XLM-targ bar is around 25, and both permute variants are very low, around 1. The Uralic group shows the mBERT-targ bar at approximately 28 and the XLM-targ bar at approximately 21, with the permute variants again being very low. The bars are not sorted, and no individual bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and error bars.
